text: Sir, we have a serious problem.
What is it? I'm about to walk into a meeting.
The company stock just crashed. Investors are pulling out, and the banks have frozen our accounts.
What? That's impossible! We made forty million dollars last quarter!
Sir, we're facing bankruptcy.
Bankruptcy? I've spent twenty years building this company! Fix it!
We've tried everything. I'm sorry.
No... No, this can't be happening.
Honey, you need to come to the hospital. There's been an accident.
What accident? What happened?
It's our son. Please, just get here.
Doctor! Where's my son? Is he okay?
Sir, we did everything we could. I'm so sorry.
No... Please, God, no. Take everything I own, but not my boy!
I don't understand. I've worked hard my entire life. I've given to charity. I've helped people. Why is God doing this to me?
Maybe you should stop pretending God cares about you. Look at what He's allowed to happen!
What am I supposed to do? Curse Him? Turn my back on Him because my life fell apart?
You've lost your company, your money, and now your son. What else is there?
I don't know anymore.
Man, I heard about everything. I'm sorry.
Thanks for coming.
But I've got to ask you something. What did you do?
What do you mean?
Nobody loses this much without doing something wrong. Maybe God is punishing you.
You think I haven't asked myself that question a thousand times?
Then maybe you should figure out what you did.
I spent my entire life believing that if I did good, good things would happen to me. Now I don't even know what to believe.
So you still believe in God?
I don't understand Him right now. I'm angry. I'm broken. I have questions I'll probably never get answers to.
Then why keep believing?
Because I never worshiped God for the money He gave me.
But He let you lose everything.
I know. And I may never understand why.
So what's left?
My faith. My memories of my son. The love I still have for my family. And the choice of what kind of man I become after all this.
You really think you can start over?
I don't know if I'll ever have another million dollars. And no amount of money will ever bring my son back.
Then what are you going to do?
Tomorrow, I'm going to get up. I'm going to help my wife through another day. I'm going to take whatever work I can find. And I'm going to keep trusting God, even when I don't understand Him.
I don't think I could do that.
Neither did I, until I had no other choice.
You know, I always thought you were blessed because you were rich.
So did I. But maybe I was confusing blessings with possessions.
What do you mean?
I thought having everything meant I had God's favor. Now I'm learning that losing everything doesn't mean I've lost His love.

And that's the lesson. Faith isn't proven when you have everything you want. It's tested when everything you depended on is taken away. Because the true measure of a man isn't what he owns when life is good, but who he chooses to become when life falls apart.
